<!-- pr-reviewer: 0beeec42ad2207c1f712622f4160925f3ca7e3fb -->
**Independent review (v0.14.0 cut), static.** I read the diff, `fanuc.cps`, `motion/src/probing.rs`, `operation/probe_op.rs`, `kinds.rs` and the golden. Verdict: **1 BLOCKING item**, plus notes.

### BLOCKING

**1. The probe programs the ball centre, but the rest of the system programs the tool tip, and nothing tells the operator.** `probe_cycle` places every move at the ball centre (`expect = contact - dir*r`; `stylus_hits` sweeps a ball of radius r about the move points). The posted G31 Z is that centre. Every other tool in this codebase posts the tip (RECOMMENDED, rotary "pivot law (1)": the posted tip is the ball centre minus r·axis). A spindle probe's H register is normally gauged to the ball's bottom/trigger point. Neither the program nor the setup sheet says H07 must be gauged to the ball centre.

Concrete case, the default op (`seed_probe`: -Z face at Z0, set G54, tolerance 0.5) with PRB-0400 (r = 2), H07 gauged to the tip:
- The seek runs from Z7 toward `G31 Z-3` (expected ball-centre trip at Z2 = contact + r). It trips when the **tip** reaches Z0, so `#5063` = 0 while `Expected` = 2.
- That gives `#190 = -2`. With tolerance 0.5, every run alarms "OUT OF TOLERANCE", so the default op cannot be used.
- With any tolerance of 2 or more, `G10 L2 P1 Z[#5223+#190]` moves G54 Z 2 mm down. Every following op then cuts 2 mm too deep: a gouge the verifier cannot see.
- XY touches also land r higher than asked. Edge mode with `depth 3` touches only 1 mm below the edge, and on a chamfered or radiused edge it touches the chamfer, which gives a wrong XY offset.

Fix one of two ways: (a) post the tip, as the other tools do (Z - r on every probe block and on the Z `Expected`, with the stylus law still sweeping the centre), or (b) keep the centre but print a program comment and a setup-sheet line saying H<n> must be gauged to the ball centre, and pin it with a test. (a) is the safer choice: it matches how the shop measures the probe.

### Checked, fine
- G31 is one-shot. `#5061-#5063` are read right after each skip and kept in `#100+3k`. The no-contact check (`IF[ABS[#506x-target]LT0.001]THEN#3000=2`) comes before any back-off, on the axis of travel. This relies on G31 ending at its target when no skip fires, which is correct.
- The back-off is incremental (`G91 G01 ... / G90`), so a part nearer than the model is never driven into. The final retract to the nominal point is an XY+Z diagonal, but in a bore both ends lie inside the clearance cylinder (the plunge only succeeds if they do), so the convex hull keeps it off the wall. Outside a face or boss the same holds within `approach`.
- `G10 L2 P(n+1)`: P1..P6 = G54..G59. It reads the active slot `#5221 + 20 x slot + axis` and writes target = active + deviation, which is right for a measurement taken in the active WCS. Golden: G54 active, `P2` (G55) from `#5221/#5222`. Correct.
- The tolerance stop is `#3000=1`. Report mode is `#3006=1`.
- The probe section starts no spindle (`sRpm > 0` guard) and no coolant. The golden has no S/M3/M8, and the previous section's M5 still closes it.
- Op-type ids: Probe is appended as tag 38, no existing row or digest tag moves, and `project/file.rs` keeps v50 (an additive word). OK.
- Other posts refuse by name (no prelude default). Pinned.
- The golden matches the PR body: bore centre with four touches, each a seek F300, `G91` back-off 1, measure F30 and back-off to centre. Mean of opposite touches, tolerance 0.5, G55 set.

### Non-blocking
- A negative target or expected value prints as a double sign, for example `IF[ABS[#5061--43]...` or `#190=[...]--30` (G54 at the part centre, a -X face). Whether a given Fanuc parses `--` in a macro expression is control-dependent. Writing `[#5061+43]`, or bracketing `[-43]`, costs nothing.
- In a bore or boss, the Y touches are made at the nominal X, not at the measured X centre. For a part off-centre in X there is a small chord error in Y (second order). Probing cycles usually re-centre between the X pair and the Y pair.
- There is no probe-on/off M-code (most spindle probes need one). This is worth a line in #173.
- The caveat that the code is unverified on a control is fair. Please carry it into the release notes.
Back to draft: an agent is merging current main (21 conflicts) and fixing the review blocker (stylus ball centre vs tool tip, review 0beeec4). Will mark ready again when gated.

Rework done: main merged (twice), review blocker from 0beeec4 fixed. Head `c7e67ce`.

**Conflict resolution** (merge `bb90a2e`, 21 files; the second sync `c7e67ce` was clean). Every file keeps both sides:
- **cl** (`path.rs`, `mod.rs`, `frame.rs`): `Toolpath` carries both `threads` (#34) and `probes`. In `TiltedFrame::world_path` the probe touches no longer clone local indices. Each touch is re-pointed through a local-to-world move map, because a flattened arc becomes several chords and would shift every later index. Its target is also mapped through the frame. A touch with no match keeps an out-of-range index, so `is_sane` refuses it at the post and it cannot turn into a plain feed.
- **post** (`cnc.rs`, `engine.rs`, `mod.rs`, `tests/post_engine.rs`): the `Record` enum has main's `Comp { wear }` and `Thread(..)` plus `Touch` / `Found` / `Retreat`, in the label, serialize and engine arms. `Dump` has both `coolant` and `probe_result`. The dump runs the touch sanity check and builds the thread brackets. I also fixed a broken line continuation in the `onProbeRetreat` refusal text.
- **app**: in `rest/ahead.rs`, a probe still cuts nothing, now on main's `path_sig` read (sig 0, no moves). `finish_clip.rs` drops threads (main) and keeps probes. `project/entity.rs` loads through `ToolpathCache::new` (#109/#153). `ProbeTouchDto` and its loader moved to a new `project/touch_dto.rs` so `entity.rs` grows by 9 lines, not 44. `turning_rapids_tests.rs` literals carry both fields.
- **motion / sim tests**: struct literals carry both fields (`sideways_rapids.rs` too: no textual conflict, but it failed to compile).
- **RECOMMENDED.md**: taken from main. This PR's entry moved unchanged to `docs/decisions/108-probe.md`.

**Blocker fix** (`2c686c6`, option (a)): the probe now programs the stylus **tip**, like every other ball tool (pivot law: centre = tip + r·axis).
- `probe_cycle` still plans on the ball centre. When it lays the moves and targets down, it shifts them by -r in Z.
- The safe plane is a tip height.
- `stylus_hits` sweeps the ball about each point raised by r, so the judged geometry is unchanged.
- A -Z face at Z20 now posts `G31 … Z15` (overtravel 5) and expects its trip at Z20, so a part where the model says sets a zero offset.
- XY expectations stay at the spindle axis.
- Pinned by `probe_op::the_posted_g31_z_is_the_tip_at_the_expected_contact` (face and bore-centre G31 Z). `each_mode_lays_down_its_touches` was updated to tip trips.
- The `nc/fanuc/probe_bore_centre.nc` golden was regenerated. The diff is exactly every Z 2 mm lower (Z27→25, Z17→15) with the safe plane Z50 unchanged; nothing else moved.
- The decision is recorded in `docs/decisions/108-probe.md`.

**Results** on the final merged tree, with its own target dir:
- `cargo test --no-run` for cl, post, sim, motion, app and ui builds.
- 28 binaries green, 663 passed, 0 failed:
  - cl, sim, motion and post libs, plus the app lib `turning_rapids` tests;
  - motion: one_descent, machining3d, pocket3d_hsm, engagement_3d, entry_arc_3d (SLOW_BINARIES skipped);
  - sim: vertical/sideways/radial rapids, overhang_laws, posed_rapids, midmove_pose;
  - post: post_engine;
  - app: probe_op, ribbon, project_roundtrip, conformance, posting, golden_cl, operations, vertical_rapid_stock, fanuc_post, pocket3d_hsm.
- clippy `-D warnings` on cl, post, sim, motion, app and ui: clean.

Still owed, as before: #171 (picking), #172, #173, #174. The non-blocking `--` double-sign note is not addressed here.

**Estimated agent cost:** ~$3.62 (rough estimate from size: 2308 changed lines)

No token usage was recorded for this PR, so this is calibrated from PRs with measured cost (our fix PRs, fix agent + review: median ~$1.20, ~$2.33 per 1,000 changed lines; floor $0.15, cap ~$3.60). For a contributor's PR it estimates what writing and reviewing it the way our agents work would cost, not what their session actually spent.

Blended upper estimate: 90 % input / 10 % output at list price (Opus 5.5 ~$5.60/M, Sonnet 5.5 ~$2.80/M, Haiku 5.5 ~$0.14/M). Cache reads make the real cost lower; main-session coordination isn't counted.
